# Course-to-feature map

<!-- Generated by backend/scripts/gen_course_mapping.py from backend/app/course_map.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Each row ties an IS-353 lecture week to the part of AEGIS USB that demonstrates it. The **CIA** column says which security property the feature protects (C = confidentiality, I = integrity, A = availability). The same table is shown in the dashboard's **About** tab.

| Week | Topic | Where it lives in AEGIS USB | CIA | Status | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | Attack taxonomy + classical crypto | MITRE ATT&CK tags on every detection; single-byte XOR de-obfuscation of hidden PE headers (a classical cipher real malware uses); entropy as frequency analysis. | I | Implemented | [`backend/app/engine/xor_detect.py`](../backend/app/engine/xor_detect.py)<br>[`backend/app/engine/entropy.py`](../backend/app/engine/entropy.py)<br>[`backend/app/engine/analyzer.py`](../backend/app/engine/analyzer.py)<br>[`backend/app/rules/usb_threats.yar`](../backend/app/rules/usb_threats.yar) |
| 3 | Symmetric crypto | AES-256-GCM quarantine vault: flagged files are copied in encrypted so they cannot execute; key from scrypt; the file hash is bound in as associated data. | C, I | Implemented | [`backend/app/core/vault.py`](../backend/app/core/vault.py)<br>[`qa_demo/test_crypto.py`](../qa_demo/test_crypto.py) |

## Honest gaps

- **Week 15, BadUSB alert:** not built. A malicious *device* that pretends to be a keyboard is invisible to a tool that only reads file contents; `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` explains the gap.
- **Week 7, Authenticode:** we check that a signature is present and well-formed, not that its certificate chain is trusted.
- **Week 14, retention:** only the intel cache is purged automatically.
